newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia indicts 12 for harassment of Serbs.
newsitem.headline: Croatia indicts 12 for harassment of Serbs.

text.p: Croatia pressed charges on Tuesday against 12 people for harassing and evicting elderly minority Serbs who returned to the homes they abandoned during war in 1995, the state agency Hina reported.

The move came only days after U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright visited Croatia and publicly criticised President Franjo Tudjman over the treatment of minority Serbs who fled en masse from the Croatian army's recapture of their rebel area.
Albright urged Tudjman to exercise moral leadership to create conditions for the return and co-existence of Serbs and Croats and said it would be "useful if some arrests were made" in the area.
Tudjman appeared to comply on Monday by giving a conciliatory speech to the Serbs in their last, soon-to-be-dissolved enclave of Eastern Slavonia and vowing to protect multi-ethnic life there.
Authorities previously blamed the evictions on embittered Croat refugees from Bosnia's 1992-95 war who were resettled in Serb houses near Kostajnica, central Croatia.
HINA did not say if the 12 indicted, one of whom is under-aged, were from Bosnia or Croatia nor what sentence they would face if convicted.
